S065.name: Obsessions
S065.description: Recurrent and persistent thoughts, urges, or images that are experienced as intrusive and unwanted, and attempts to ignore or suppress them.

subtypes.Contamination Obsessions: Recurrent and intrusive worries about contamination, germs, or dirt.
subtypes.Pathological Doubt: Pathological doubt regarding safety or mistakes, such as whether doors are locked or gas valves are closed.
subtypes.Symmetry and Exactness Obsessions: A strong urge that items must be lined up exactly or be symmetrical.
subtypes.Forbidden or Taboo Thoughts: Intrusive thoughts involving aggressive (harming others), sexual, or religious content that are prohibited.
subtypes.Somatic Obsessions: Persistent and specific fear that one might have a serious disease.

S066.name: Compulsions
S066.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to an obsession or to prevent anxiety/distress; clearly excessive or not realistically connected.

subtypes.Cleaning or Washing Compulsions: Repetitive acts to remove contamination, such as hand washing, showering, or excessive cleaning.
subtypes.Checking Compulsions: Repeatedly checking items like door locks, gas stoves, or switches to prevent danger.
subtypes.Ordering and Arranging Compulsions: Organizing objects in a specific order or at a precise angle to reduce anxiety.
subtypes.Mental Acts: Mental rituals performed internally, such as praying, counting, or repeating specific words silently.
subtypes.Repeating Rituals: Repeating specific actions (e.g., standing up, passing through a door) a set number of times.

patient_info.stressor: Sarah’s divorce disrupted the carefully organized home routines that had supported her demanding analytics work, leaving her solely responsible for the house, garden, finances, and the social calendar she had once shared. In the months that followed, intrusive unwanted thoughts about making irreversible mistakes in documents, locks, bills, and data releases began to intrude during workdays and quiet evenings alike. Her attempts to neutralize those thoughts through repeated reviewing and other rituals expanded until project timelines slipped, salsa nights and kayaking plans were canceled, and colleagues noticed she was staying late without completing deliverables. After missing a major community-development reporting deadline, Sarah directly contacted a psychiatrist through her health plan because she feared she could no longer manage the pattern on her own.

S065.name: Obsessions
S065.description: Recurrent and persistent thoughts, urges, or images that are experienced as intrusive and unwanted, and attempts to ignore or suppress them.
S065.manifestation: I came in because I keep getting these awful, unwanted thoughts that I’ve missed something critical—a wrong number in a data release, an unlocked back door, a bill paid from the wrong account—and even when I know I checked it, my mind won’t let go of the possibility that I’ve caused a disaster.

S066.name: Compulsions
S066.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to an obsession or to prevent anxiety/distress; clearly excessive or not realistically connected.
S066.manifestation: To calm myself down I end up reopening spreadsheets, rereading emails line by line, checking locks and payment confirmations over and over in a set order until it feels 'safe,' and some nights I’m still at my desk hours later with nothing actually finished.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I’ve fallen behind on major work deadlines because I stay late reviewing things but still don’t finish, and I’ve stopped going to salsa nights or kayaking because I can’t get away from the checking and reviewing in time.
